alerts.title: Viral Load Monitoring Schedule
alerts.message: Guidelines specify a viral load monitoring schedule of every 3 months for pregnant women. The patient initiated ART 10 weeks ago and is 22 weeks pregnant. Her latest viral load is 89 copies/mL, indicating suppression. However, the next viral load test is not documented in the clinician's plan, creating a monitoring gap for this high-risk period.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule the next viral load test as per the 3-monthly schedule for pregnant women.

alerts.title: Creatinine Rise on TDF
alerts.message: The patient's creatinine has risen from a baseline of 0.8 mg/dL to 1.1 mg/dL after 10 weeks on a TDF-containing regimen (TLD), with a corresponding eGFR of 78 mL/min/1.73m2. TDF is a known cause of renal impairment. However, pregnancy itself can cause physiological changes in renal function and serum creatinine. The absence of proteinuria on urinalysis is reassuring but does not rule out drug-related toxicity.

evidence.recommended_action: Monitor renal function closely. Consider TDF alternatives if creatinine continues to rise or if other signs of renal impairment appear.

alerts.title: DTG and Iron Supplement Interaction
alerts.message: Guidelines highlight a potential interaction between DTG and divalent cation-containing medications like iron supplements. The patient is pregnant and taking ferrous sulfate. This co-administration can reduce DTG absorption, risking virological failure and mother-to-child transmission.

evidence.recommended_action: Advise patient to take iron supplements at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after DTG dose.
